Atlantis, The Palm.notes: Do not confuse this property with its newer sister resort, Atlantis The Royal, which sits next door on the Palm but is a separate, more adult-skewed hotel with its own restaurant line-up. Restaurant list here is a representative selection of confirmed, currently operating venues rather than the full count (the resort advertises around 30 restaurants, bars and lounges in total, and this can change). Exact room square metreages vary slightly by source and may have been refreshed since some listings were published, so treat sizes as approximate.

Atlantis The Royal.notes: Some celebrity-chef venues (La Mar by Gastón Acurio and Dinner by Heston Blumenthal) have been reported as paused at various points in 2025-26, so they've been left off this list — worth a direct check with the hotel before promising a specific restaurant for a milestone dinner. Room category names (Sky Terrace Suites, Family Terrace, Sky Pool Villa, Signature Penthouses) are confirmed via the official site and hotel documentation, but exact square footage wasn't consistently published, so sizes have been left out rather than guessed.

Address Beach Resort.notes: Some third-party listings mention additional outsourced venues (DREAMS, Dreams of Garden, Via Toledo, Li'Brasil) but naming was inconsistent across sources, so these were left out in favour of the restaurants confirmed with their own current pages. The rooftop infinity pool has a minimum age and restricted morning hours for in-house guests (roughly 7am-11am) — worth flagging to families expecting all-day rooftop access.

Address Downtown.notes: Room dimensions and sleeping capacities are drawn from third-party booking listings rather than the hotel's own site, so treat exact square footage as indicative. Older articles mention venues such as Zeta, The Galliard, STK and 99 Sushi Bar at this property — these do not appear on the hotel's current official restaurant list and have been excluded. There is no private beach at this property; nearest beach access would require a drive to a sister Address or Jumeirah property.

Address Beach Resort Fujairah.notes: SALiA appears as 'temporarily closed' on one Address Hotels booking page but is described as operating (dinner service, closed Mondays) by several other current sources including Virgin Atlantic and On the Beach — worth a quick live-availability check before promising it. Could not confirm named spa awards, a specific room count breakdown beyond general totals, or an official 'bed and breakfast' package name, though breakfast can be added for a fee on room-only bookings.

Al Maha, a Luxury Collection Desert Reso.notes: Minimum child age is reported inconsistently across booking channels (figures from 6 to 11 appear on different OTAs), but the hotel's own Marriott page and most specialist tour operators state 10 years and above, and this is the figure to quote to customers. Al Diwaan is the resort's only restaurant — worth telling repeat-night guests up front so they're not expecting variety. Some third-party listings still reference a fifth suite category or slightly different villa names; the current Marriott site confirms four categories — Bedouin, Royal, Emirates and Presidential Villas.

Ajman Hotel by Blazon Hotels.notes: The hotel's own website (hotelajman.com) is currently showing a mix of 'Ajman Hotel by Blazon Hotels' branding and newer 'Dusit Ajman Resort & Villas' branding, suggesting a management or brand transition is underway as of early 2026. Some previously reported venues (an all-day dining outlet once called Sabella's, a 'Blazon Lounge') may have been renamed or discontinued as part of this — Café Naseem appears to be the current all-day dining name. Worth a direct call to the hotel to confirm branding and open venues before a client books, and to check whether the bowling alley referenced in older write-ups is still operating.

Al Wathba, a Luxury Collection Desert Re.notes: Bait Al Hanine, the resort's main all-day dining restaurant, is listed as temporarily closed on the official Marriott dining page, so it's excluded from the restaurant list above — worth checking its status before promising it to guests. A lobby lounge called Hayaakom appears in older marketing material but is not listed on the current official dining page, so it may have closed or been folded into another venue. The spa was known as Talise Spa when the property operated under Jumeirah; it now trades as Saray Spa under Marriott's Luxury Collection ownership. Room sizes are approximate and taken from a mix of the official site and OTA listings.

Anantara Mina Al Arab Ras Al Khaimah Res.notes: Some third-party listings still show slightly older branding as 'Anantara Mina Ras Al Khaimah Resort' rather than the full 'Mina Al Arab' name used in the brief — this is the same property. Pool bar and lobby lounge/bar are confirmed to exist but I could not confirm a specific venue name for either, so they're omitted from the restaurant list rather than guessed. Half board and all-inclusive options were not clearly confirmed on the official site, so only room only and bed & breakfast are listed.

Anantara The Palm Dubai Resort.notes: Room sizes and villa counts are drawn from older but consistent third-party listings (Anantara itself doesn't publish exact square metreage on its current rooms page), so treat exact figures as indicative rather than guaranteed current. Restaurant list of seven venues (Mekong, Bushman's, The Beach House, Crescendo, Revo Café, Mai Bar, The Lotus Lounge) is confirmed directly from the hotel's own site. Note that on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays the resort's on-site parking is reserved for hotel guests, so anyone visiting just for a restaurant booking needs to use street parking or arrive by taxi.

Banyan Tree Dubai.notes: The resort opened in its Banyan Tree form in November 2023, replacing Caesars Palace Dubai. Earlier press around launch mentioned additional venues (Havana Social Club, The Shack) that no longer appear on the hotel's own current dining page, so these have been left out. The kids' club (Club Tropicool) is physically located within the neighbouring sister hotel Delano rather than on the Banyan Tree site itself, a short walk away — worth flagging to families booking on the assumption it's on-property. Room category names can vary slightly between the hotel's own site and third-party booking sites; the six listed here are the ones consistently confirmed across the official site and multiple independent sources.

Barracuda Beach Resort.notes: Core facts (room categories, restaurants, pool, location) are confirmed from the hotel's own site (barracuda.ae) and consistent across booking platforms. Meal plan options are inferred from breakfast being sold as an add-on on third-party sites rather than confirmed board categories on the official site — worth double-checking at time of booking. Several recent guest reports flag that the lagoon has a tidal beach with limited swimmable water at low tide, which is worth flagging to families expecting a conventional sand-and-sea beach. No spa, kids' club or gym could be confirmed, so none are listed.

Centara Mirage Beach Resort Dubai.notes: Room sizes and exact category names are taken from the hotel's own accommodation page; some third-party sites list slightly different sub-variants (Mirage, Build-A-Bear Edition, bunk-bed options) of the same base categories, which I've kept out to avoid inventing sub-types not clearly confirmed. Distances to Dubai Marina are estimated from general Dubai Islands drive times rather than a single confirmed source, so treat that figure as indicative.

Conrad Abu Dhabi Etihad Towers.notes: Older sources (Virgin Atlantic, third-party sites) list additional venues such as Tori No Su and VaKaVa, but these don't appear on the hotel's current official Hilton dining navigation, so they've been left out in case they've closed or rebranded. Half board, full board and all-inclusive are not advertised for this property, which is a city-style hotel rather than a resort. Level 45 areas restrict under-15s after 5pm, worth flagging to families booking executive rooms.

Coral Beach Resort Sharjah.notes: Room and restaurant names confirmed against the official HMH Hotel Group site. Some third-party booking sites reference an 'infinity edge pool' or a 'Deluxe Room City View' category not named on the official site, so these were left out. Sharjah is a dry emirate and this property is alcohol-free, which is worth flagging to guests expecting a bar.

Crowne Plaza Abu Dhabi Yas Island.notes: Pool count is inconsistent across sources: the hotel's own IHG page states one outdoor pool plus a kids' pool at the property itself, while some references mention wider access to pools across the Yas Plaza hotel collection. Restaurant count also varies by source (yasisland.com says five on-site restaurants, IHG's own page references 21 venues across the whole Yas Plaza collection) — the five listed here are specific to this hotel. Beach access is to Cyan Beach, shared with the Yas Plaza cluster, not a private beach exclusive to this hotel.

DoubleTree by Hilton Resort & Spa Marjan.notes: Room count and category names vary slightly across booking channels (some list closer to 600 rooms, others over 700, and naming for suites/villas differs by site) - the categories above are the ones confirmed on Hilton's own site. The hotel states 13 restaurants and bars in total; only the currently-open, clearly-named venues confirmed across the official site and reputable travel sites are listed here. All-inclusive and half-board packages are commonly sold by tour operators for this property, though exact inclusions vary by operator.

Fairmont Ajman.notes: Room size figures come directly from the hotel's own room pages, though a couple of categories (Family Room and Two Bedroom Suite) share near-identical template text on the official site, so treat exact square metreages as approximate rather than guaranteed per category. Golf is offered via an off-site partnership with Al Zorah Golf Club, not a course on property. Some third-party sites list slightly different restaurant counts (6-8), likely reflecting seasonal openings/closures of pop-up or outdoor venues; the six named here are consistently confirmed on the hotel's own dining page.

Fairmont Bab Al Bahr.notes: Room category names and descriptions are drawn directly from the Fairmont website, though a couple of listings (Junior Suite, Penthouse Suite, private-pool villas) exist but weren't detailed enough in search results to write confidently — worth a call to the hotel to check current villa availability if a guest wants an in-room pool. Some third-party sites list slightly different room counts (366–369); the hotel's own site consistently says 366.

Fairmont Fujairah Beach Resort.notes: The evening seafood restaurant appears on the official site as Copper Lobster; some older listings still call it Sea Grill, so use Copper Lobster as current. The kids club is named Little Sailors Club on the Fairmont site (ages 4-8) though a couple of third-party pages call it Sun Family Kids Club — Little Sailors is the name used consistently on the hotel's own dining/activities pages. Airport distances vary between sources (official site puts Fujairah Airport at ~59km/RAK at 38km; a booking site suggests RAK is nearer at ~26mi), so treat exact km figures as approximate.

Fairmont The Palm.notes: No waterpark on site, which some marketing lists elsewhere miss. Complimentary Kids Club time is generally capped at around two hours a day under current family packages, with extra time chargeable. Some third-party sites still list a restaurant called Blowfish; current official channels don't clearly confirm it, so it's been left out. Restaurant and pool counts vary slightly between official copy (11 restaurants and bars, 8 pools) and OTA listings (10 restaurants, 4 pools) — likely a difference in how bars/lounges and split pool areas are counted.

Hampton by Hilton Marjan Island.notes: CLAW BBQ and Karma Kafé by Buddha-Bar are a la carte venues charged outside the all-inclusive plan (guests typically get a discount there instead). Some reviewers describe the beach and pool as feeling crowded when the hotel is full, worth flagging to families expecting resort-scale space for 515 rooms.

Hilton Abu Dhabi Yas Island.notes: Room counts vary slightly across sources (544 vs 545 including 59 suites) — not significant for booking purposes. Reviewers note high food and drink prices on site and busy pools in peak periods, and mixed feedback on noise given the promenade location, worth flagging to families wanting a quieter stay. The wider Yas Bay promenade itself has dozens of additional independent restaurants within walking distance, separate from the hotel's own venues listed here.

FIVE Palm Jumeirah.notes: Could not confirm current board-basis options (half board/all-inclusive) beyond room only and B&B, so left these off rather than guess. Some third-party listings mention additional outlets (e.g. Blvd, Roar) but these weren't confirmed on the hotel's own site, so they've been excluded. Villas and penthouses are marketed partly as residences/long-stay product alongside standard hotel rooms — worth flagging to clients booking a villa that the vibe and access differs slightly from the main tower rooms.

InterContinental Fujairah Resort.notes: Some sources list 'three culinary destinations' while IHG's own FAQ says six restaurants; I've only named the four venues I can confirm currently exist and operate (Nama, Drift, Horizon Lounge & Bar, Beach Bar) — there may be an additional pool bar or food truck outlet not consistently confirmed across sources, so I've left it out rather than guess. Room sizes for suites vary quite widely (up to 245sqm) depending on category, worth checking the specific suite type before booking for a larger family.

JA Hatta Fort Hotel.notes: Reported room counts vary slightly across sources (50-54) reflecting refurbishments and the newer Terra Cabin additions - treat exact inventory as approximate. Meal plan options beyond room only and bed & breakfast (e.g. half board) could not be firmly confirmed on the official site, so were left off rather than guessed. Sunset Terrace operates seasonally in winter, per the hotel's own description.

Jumeirah Al Qasr.notes: Room sizes and exact suite hierarchy vary slightly across booking sites; figures given are the most commonly cited. The resort's total restaurant count is often quoted as 'over 40' across the whole Madinat Jumeirah complex, not all within Al Qasr itself — I've only listed venues confirmed as being at Al Qasr specifically. Meal plan availability can vary by rate and season, so worth confirming half board dine-around terms at time of booking.

Jumeirah Al Naseem.notes: Some older write-ups still list Katsuya as the Japanese restaurant here; current sources point to Kayto (Japanese-Peruvian) as the venue now operating in that space, so it's worth double-checking the live dining list before promising a specific outlet. The hotel's own dining page shows some venues marked temporarily closed at times, so confirm opening status closer to the stay.

JA The Resort.notes: JA The Resort is made up of three separately branded hotels — JA Beach Hotel, JA Palm Tree Court and JA Lake View Hotel — which share the grounds, beach and most activities but have their own room categories and some of their own restaurants. Room and dining details above are drawn mainly from JA Beach Hotel and JA Palm Tree Court, which had the clearest confirmed detail; JA Lake View Hotel's specific room category names could not be confirmed and have been left out rather than guessed.

Jumeirah Saadiyat Island Resort.notes: Room and villa naming varies slightly between the hotel's own site, tour operators and OTAs (e.g. 'Ocean Deluxe King Room' vs 'Deluxe Room (Ocean)'), so treat the headings above as the commonly used names rather than a definitive current rate-code list. Some older sources mention a rooftop cigar lounge and a Lobster Lounge as separate outlets; these were not clearly confirmed as current standalone venues so have been left out. Total room count is cited inconsistently across sources (285–296), likely reflecting different points in time or inclusion of villas.

Lapita, Dubai Parks and Resorts, Autogra.notes: Important: at various points through 2026 both Dubai Parks and Resorts and this hotel have faced closures — a regional security-related shutdown in early 2026 and separately announced renovation works affecting parts of the year (dates cited by different booking sites range from March through mid-September 2026). Given the whole appeal of this property is park-inclusive packages, confirm directly with the hotel or Marriott which theme parks and hotel venues are operating before quoting this to a family. Room counts also vary slightly by source (504 vs 612 in older listings) — 504 rooms including 60 suites and 3 villas is the figure the hotel itself and most recent sources use.

Le Méridien Al Aqah Beach Resort.notes: The hotel underwent a partial rooms renovation starting June 2024 running for around 15 months, covering the Deluxe Sea View and Superior Sea View with Balcony categories — worth checking which block a booking falls in if noise or finish matters. Some third-party sites reference a rooftop bar (Astro's) and additional outlets like Swaad or a lounge called Layali by Swaad, but these weren't confirmed on the hotel's own Marriott pages, so they've been left out rather than guessed at. Total restaurant and bar count varies by source (five to nine depending on how outlets are counted); the five listed here are the ones consistently confirmed on the official site.

Le Méridien Mina Seyahi Beach Resort & W.notes: This hotel sits within the wider Mina Seyahi complex alongside the Westin Dubai Mina Seyahi and W Dubai - Mina Seyahi. Some restaurants, the spa and the waterpark are shared facilities across the resorts rather than exclusive to Le Méridien, which is worth flagging to guests expecting a fully private footprint. Room sizes are approximate and vary slightly by source.

Mövenpick Resort Al Marjan Island.notes: The hotel's own materials describe the offshore attraction as a 'floating water park' built by Wibit rather than a fixed splash park with slides — it's an inflatable structure on the sea, not a land-based waterpark, worth clarifying to customers expecting a Wild Wadi-style park. Kids-stay-free and specific pricing/offers were not verified and are excluded per policy. Meal plan list is based on how OTAs and the hotel describe dining structure rather than a single definitive board-basis page.

Park Hyatt Abu Dhabi Hotel and Villas.notes: Restaurant count varies across sources (three to six venues quoted); this profile lists the six venues confirmed by name on Hyatt's own dining page. Room categories listed are those named directly on hyatt.com; several other suite and villa variants exist but weren't individually confirmed with enough detail to include.

One&Only Royal Mirage.notes: The Palace wing is currently closed for refurbishment according to the hotel's own site, which affects room stock and has taken some legacy Palace restaurants (Olives, the old Kasbar nightclub) out of regular rotation, so these were left out. A new restaurant, Nayara (Levantine), is due to reopen in winter 2026 but wasn't included as it isn't open yet. Some third-party listings still reference older venue names (Nina, Kasbar, The Courtyards) that may have closed or paused with the Palace works, so it's worth confirming current opening status with the hotel directly before promising a specific restaurant to a guest.

Riu Dubai.notes: Restaurant and bar names are confirmed (Al-Andalus, Spices, The Palm, The Moon as restaurants; The Pearl, Shamal, Spike, Oasis and Coral among the bars), but exact current bar line-up wasn't independently verified on the live official site beyond secondary sources, so I kept bars out of the named restaurant list. Reviews are mixed on beach sand quality (some describe shell/pebble underfoot) and there was construction on the neighbouring plot reported through 2025 - worth checking current status before booking. Room sizes and bed configurations come from third-party travel agent listings rather than the hotel's own site, so treat exact square metres as approximate.

Mysk Kingfisher Retreat.notes: Could not confirm the hotel's own website URL directly in search results, though it operates under the Mysk by Shaza / Sharjah Collection brand (Shurooq-developed). Sharjah is dry throughout, so this property serves no alcohol at all - flag this to guests. Some reviews mention that guests are sometimes transferred by golf buggy rather than boat when roadworks or tides affect the crossing, so it's worth setting expectations that the 'boat arrival' isn't always guaranteed on every visit.

Qasr Al Sarab Desert Resort by Anantara.notes: The on-file one-liner describes this as a '90-minute drive past Liwa' — that understates it considerably. Every source, including the hotel's own site, puts it at 2.5 hours from Abu Dhabi city and 3.5 hours from Dubai, so the copy should be corrected before publishing. Al Falaj closes seasonally each summer (reopening October), which matters for anyone booking a warm-weather weekend. Room and villa counts vary slightly by source (roughly 205-207 keys across categories), so treat exact inventory figures as approximate rather than quoting a precise number.

Rixos Bab Al Bahr.notes: Room and restaurant counts vary between sources (some cite 627-715 rooms, 14-27 restaurants and bars group-wide across Rixos properties) — the figures used here are the ones consistently confirmed for this specific property. Independent reviews (Oyster, Holiday Gems) note the pools and buffet can be crowded and noisy at peak times, and à la carte restaurant reservations should be made early as slots fill quickly.

Rixos Premium Saadiyat Island.notes: Restaurant and bar counts vary between sources (some say six restaurants and five or six bars, others cite higher combined totals) — the six named restaurants above (Turquoise, People's, Mermaid, L'Olivo, Aja & Teppanyaki, Orient) are consistently confirmed across the hotel's own site and multiple travel agent pages, so these are the ones used. One source lists Orient as adults-only in the evening; worth double-checking at time of booking if travelling with children who want to dine there. A room count of 288 rooms and 12 villas is well corroborated; a figure of '1,700 rooms' appearing on one Rixos.com page is clearly a templating error carrying over copy from Rixos Phu Quoc and has been disregarded.

Rove La Mer Beach.notes: Only two Rover Room categories and three on-site food and drink outlets could be confirmed directly from the hotel and major booking sites — nearby independent restaurants at J1 Beach (Masti, Chouchou, Baoli, Aprons & Hammers, Kaimana) are steps away and popular with guests but are not part of the hotel itself, so they've been left out. The area was formerly branded La Mer and has been undergoing redevelopment as J1 Beach, which may mean some construction noise nearby depending on timing.

Rixos The Palm Dubai Hotel & Suites.notes: Restaurant naming has shifted over the years across sources (older material references Bodrum, Toro Loco Steakhouse, Salt and Meat Point as additional venues), so I've stuck to the six venues confirmed in the hotel's own July 2024 F&B materials rather than list every name that has ever appeared. Room sizes are drawn from OTA listings rather than a single hotel room-type page, so treat exact square metreage as approximate. Could not confirm current star rating source beyond the '5 star' figure widely used by booking sites.

Saadiyat Rotana Resort & Villas.notes: Restaurant count varies slightly across sources (some say 6, 7 or 8 dining outlets/bars); I've only named the four venues I could consistently confirm by name — Si Ristorante Italiano & Bar, Hamilton's Gastropub, Turtle Bay Bar & Grill and Sim Sim. There are also unnamed pool and beach bars mentioned by booking sites. Aladdin's Cave kids' club age range is quoted inconsistently (4-12 in most places, up to 16 on one Etihad page), so check current age bands before booking. All-inclusive appears as a possible package on some booking sites but I couldn't confirm it as a standing board basis, so it's left off.

Sheraton Sharjah Beach Resort & Spa.notes: Room category names and sizes come from a mix of the Marriott site and third-party agents (Junior Suite, Club Deluxe Suite, Royal Suite details are best available but worth double-checking current sqm/bedding at time of booking). Some sources list five vs six dining venues; Link Café/Al Mahatta appear to overlap in naming across sources, so confirm current café/lounge branding before publishing final copy. Confirmed alcohol-free status from multiple independent sources including guest reviews.

Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri, Abu Dhabi.notes: Sources disagree on the current restaurant count - the hotel's own homepage currently states 4 restaurants and bars, while a 2025-dated Tripadvisor listing cites 7. I've only listed venues confirmed by the hotel's own site or consistently repeated across recent third-party sources; Hoi An and Pearls & Caviar are well documented historically but weren't visible on the live official dining page at time of research, so worth a quick check before publishing for a specific date. Room category names and sizes are drawn from a mix of the official site and long-standing partner listings (Virtuoso, Etihad), so double-check exact current names if precision matters for a booking.

Sandy Beach Hotel & Resort.notes: Room and restaurant details are drawn from the hotel's own site (sandybeach.ae) and consistent secondary sources, but total room counts vary widely across booking sites (from around 96 to over 150), so treat that figure loosely. Could not confirm a formal kids' club, spa, or half board/full board/all-inclusive options — breakfast appears to be bookable separately on some rates rather than always bundled. Some scraped listings for 'Sandy Beach Resort' online actually describe unrelated properties in Greece and the US, so these were excluded.

The Ajman Saray, a Luxury Collection Res.notes: Some older listings refer to the spa as GOCO Spa while the hotel's own current site calls it Zihn Spa — used the Marriott-site name as current. Room size figures are drawn from OTA listings rather than the hotel's own page, so treat them as approximate. Ramadan hours and outlet availability can change seasonally, as the hotel itself notes.

The Chedi Al Bait, Sharjah.notes: No alcohol is served anywhere on the property as Sharjah is a dry emirate — worth flagging to guests upfront. There is no beach on the property itself; the hotel offers a complimentary shuttle to a public beach rather than private beach access, despite some third-party listings implying otherwise. No dedicated kids' club was found, and the hotel and press coverage both suggest it suits couples and families with older children better than those with toddlers. Room category names have shifted over time (some older listings use 'Chedi Grand Suite' where the current site says 'Heritage Royal Suite') — the names used here reflect the hotel's current live pages.

The Cove Rotana Resort.notes: Room and villa counts vary between sources (204 vs 349 rooms, 36 vs 40+ villas), likely reflecting renovations or re-categorisation over time, so exact inventory should be confirmed with the hotel before quoting. Some listings reference an older sub-brand called 'The Village at Cove Rotana' with its own Veranda restaurant, which may now be fully absorbed into the main resort rather than marketed separately — did not include it as a standalone venue given the uncertainty. Spa is run through Bodylines Fitness & Wellness Club rather than a separate named spa brand.

The Ritz-Carlton, Dubai.notes: Amaseena, the hotel's Middle Eastern restaurant, is listed on the official site as temporarily closed, so it has been left out of the restaurants list. Caravan and The Gulf Pavilion are also named on the official dining page but with too little confirmed detail to describe accurately, so they've been omitted rather than guessed at. Room category names vary slightly across booking sites; the ones used here match the hotel's own site and closely aligned third-party listings.

The Ritz-Carlton Ras Al Khaimah, Al Wadi.notes: Farmhouse by Syrco, the resort's signature restaurant, is temporarily closed from 27 July 2026 for renovation and is expected to reopen around October 2026 — worth flagging to anyone booking before then. There is no beach on the property itself; sea swimming is via complimentary guest access to the sister Ritz-Carlton beach resort roughly 20 minutes away. Room category names (Al Rimal, Al Khaimah, Al Sahari, Al Sarab, Signature Villas) are confirmed as existing, though exact size specs beyond the two-bedroom Signature Villa's pool size were not all independently verified on the official site.

The St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort, Ab.notes: Guest rooms and suites are being refreshed in phases from June to mid-October 2026, with a further phase planned for 2027; the Adult Pool and Sandcastle Kids' Club were also listed as under refresh for part of that period, so it's worth confirming current status at time of booking. Some third-party sources reference an additional venue (variously called MAZI or Sophia Abu Dhabi) that may have opened or rebranded since the six-restaurant count was last confirmed on the hotel's own site — left out here as it couldn't be verified as currently open.

The WB Abu Dhabi, Curio Collection by Hi.notes: Spa branding is unconfirmed on the hotel's own site (referred to generically as 'our spa'), so I've avoided naming it as Eforea despite one third-party source using that name. Theme park inclusion is typically one park per person per night — confirm exactly which parks (Warner Bros. World, Yas Waterworld, Ferrari World) are covered on the specific rate, as SeaWorld Abu Dhabi is sometimes excluded. A couple of recent reviews mention hallway soundproofing and pool-area upkeep worth flagging to guests who are sensitive to wear and tear.

Vida Beach Resort Umm Al Quwain.notes: Star rating is inconsistent across sources — third-party sites (Tripadvisor, Booking.com) list it as 5-star, but keeping to the 4-star figure on file since that's what's specified. The rooftop bar SoCal appears on the official Vida site's own restaurant page as 'temporarily closed' as of the most recent crawl, even though it's still listed among the resort's four dining spots elsewhere on the same site — worth a quick check with the hotel before promising guests a rooftop evening. Dining is genuinely limited to around four venues, so set expectations accordingly for longer stays.

W Abu Dhabi - Yas Island.notes: Pappas Taverna is listed as temporarily closed on the hotel's own Marriott dining page, so it has been left out of the restaurant list. The hotel has no private beach of its own — guests get complimentary shuttle access and vouchers for the separate Yas Beach Club nearby, which is worth flagging to anyone assuming a beachfront stay. Half board and full board options were not confirmed and have been excluded from meal plans.

Waldorf Astoria Ras Al Khaimah.notes: Room counts vary by source: the official Hilton site states 203 rooms and suites, though some third-party agents quote 346 across 14 categories — I've gone with the Hilton figure as the more reliable one. Sijar Lounge (cigar and cocktail lounge) is mentioned by some tour operators but doesn't appear on the current official Hilton dining list, so it's been left out pending confirmation it's still open under that name.

Bab Al Shams, A Rare Finds Desert Resort.notes: Some outdoor venues (Al Hadheerah, Ninive) run seasonally and close over the hottest summer months, so confirm what's open before booking a summer stay. Sources vary slightly on exact room count (113–123) — the hotel's own material and most third-party listings say 115.

Burj Al Arab Jumeirah.notes: Older sources still reference an on-site 'Sinbad's Kids Club' and a restaurant called Scape; current official material points to Sal Beach Club as the outdoor terrace venue and describes kids' club access via sister Jumeirah properties, so I've kept the family-club language general rather than naming a specific on-site club I couldn't confirm is still running. Suite square metreages vary slightly between third-party sources and should be checked against the live jumeirah.com suite pages before quoting exact figures.

Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental, Abu D.notes: The hotel's EP Club (the members'-style suite lounge referenced in some older room descriptions) has recently closed; its perks have been folded into general suite benefits, so avoid promoting it as a standalone amenity. Room size figures are only confirmed for the Sea View Suite, Two-Bedroom Palace Suite and Family Sea View Suite - other categories are described qualitatively rather than with exact square metreage.

Sofitel Dubai The Palm.notes: Room and restaurant names are taken from the hotel's own site and Accor's Sofitel page, which list slightly different outlet counts (10-12 restaurants and bars depending on the source) — this is likely down to how bars versus restaurants are counted rather than venues closing. Half board and full board options were not clearly confirmed on the hotel's own channels, so only room only and bed & breakfast are listed here; it would be worth double-checking current board options directly with the hotel before quoting a specific plan.

Jumeirah Beach Hotel.notes: Room and restaurant details are consistent across the hotel's own site, Jumeirah-affiliated tour operators (Kuoni, Tropical Sky, Prestbury) and a late-2025 press review, though exact total room counts vary slightly by source (598 to 618). Kitchen Connect is a recent rebrand of the former Latitude restaurant, and some Al Bahar Villas have been recently refreshed - worth checking which villa category is current at time of booking. Older sources still reference a 'Sinbad's Club' or 'J Club' kids club name; the hotel's own current site calls it the Jumeirah Circle kids club, which is what should be used.
